model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of six different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 10^3 (i.e., 1 to 1000). The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and uses a logarithmic scale with tick marks at 0, 10^1 (10), 10^2 (100), and 10^3 (1000). The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and spans from 40% to 65% with major grid lines every 5 percentage points. Each method is represented by a distinct line with a unique color and marker: Base (black circles), MEND (brown diamonds), FT (blue triangles), MEMIT (purple circles), IKE (red triangles), and ROME (green squares). All lines show an increasing trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases. At the lowest co-occurrence number (near 1), ROME starts at approximately 51%, MEMIT and MEND at around 44%, IKE at about 43%, FT at roughly 40%, and Base at approximately 39%. As co-occurrence increases, ROME reaches about 66% at 10^3, while MEND and MEMIT both reach approximately 56%, IKE reaches about 49%, FT reaches around 48%, and Base plateaus at about 44%. The ROME method consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers, followed by MEND and MEMIT, while Base remains the lowest throughout.
